supporting_observations.claim: The alert describes repeated failed domain logons involving svc-ledger around 13:40 UTC on 2026-10-06, but provides no event-level records or identifiers to verify the logons.

The change calendar says svc-ledger's password was scheduled for rotation at 13:30 UTC and the LedgerSync job must then be updated manually. This could plausibly relate to failures from a job that re-authenticates every minute, but the evidence does not establish that it caused the alerted activity.
Winsec and Sysmon collection were unavailable on both DC-SUN-01 and FILE-SUN-01 from 13:30 to 14:20 UTC, overlapping the alert time and preventing review of relevant host events.

known_telemetry_limitations: Winsec and Sysmon records are unavailable for DC-SUN-01 and FILE-SUN-01 during 13:30–14:20 UTC on 2026-10-06.
No event-level authentication records, source details, or record IDs for the alerted failures were provided.
claims_not_established: Whether the reported failures occurred as described, and their exact count, timestamps, logon types, or status codes.
Whether the failures originated from the expected LedgerSync job on FILE-SUN-01 or from another source.
Whether the scheduled password rotation caused the failures or whether any successful logon or subsequent misuse occurred.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover or obtain DC-SUN-01 authentication records for 13:20–14:20 UTC, including account, source host/address, logon type, status codes, and any successful logons involving svc-ledger.
Recover or obtain FILE-SUN-01 process and authentication records for the same period to determine whether LedgerSync generated the attempts and when its credentials were updated.
Obtain the password-rotation and job-update audit trail, including the time and operator or process responsible.
